subproblems.title: Monotonicity formula with ‖δV‖ ≤ Λ μ_V (Simon 8.3.3)
subproblems.statement: (Simon Ch. 8, 3.3; exactly the contract Prop MonotonicityFormula.) For all N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N and every n-varifold V on U (SimonGMT Varifold N n U; U is open): let V have locally bounded first variation in U, let x ∈ ℝ^N and ρ0 > 0 with the open ball B°_{ρ0}(x) = ball x ρ0 ⊆ U, let Λ ≥ 0, and assume ‖δV‖(B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·μ_V(B_ρ(x)) for all 0 < ρ < ρ0, where B_ρ(x) = closedBall x ρ, μ_V = V.weight and ‖δV‖ = variationMeasure V. Then (i) ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ})·μ_V(B_ρ(x))/ofReal(ρ)^n is monotone non-decreasing on (0, ρ0) (values in [0,∞]); (ii) there is θ ∈ [0,∞] with θ ≠ ∞ and HasDensity n μ_V x θ, i.e. densityRatio n μ_V x ρ = μ_V(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ)^n) → θ as ρ ↓ 0, where ω_n = unitBallVolume n; and (iii) for all 0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0: θ ≤ ofReal(e^{Λσ})·densityRatio n μ_V x σ and ofReal(e^{Λσ})·densityRatio n μ_V x σ + ω_n^{-1}·normalDefect V x (B_ρ(x) ∖ B_σ(x)) ≤ ofReal(e^{Λρ})·densityRatio n μ_V x ρ, where normalDefect V x A = ∫_{A×G(N,n)} ofReal(|(y − x) − p_S(y − x)|²/|y − x|^{n+2}) dV(y,S) (integrand 0 at y = x).
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory, Ch. 8, 3.1–3.3 (printed pp. 210–211), proved “by essentially the same computation as in §4 of Ch. 4” (Ch. 4, 3.1–3.6 and 4.7) with the radial test field X_y = γ(r)(y − x). The argument below is extracted from the parent node's accepted proof (its common radial computation and its Part A) with all details filled in; it is self-contained. Errata/normalisations: (i) the printed 3.3 is a subtraction; it is stated here additively in [0,∞], which is equivalent because every term is finite (B_ρ(x) is a compact subset of U); (ii) the sign of δV(X) in the radial identity is −δV(X) (SimonGMT Chapter08/WeightedRadialIdentity.lean, header); only |δV(X)| is used below, so the sign is irrelevant. The two first-variation inputs (‖δV‖ is the Riesz measure; the polar representation, Simon 2.6) are kernel-checked SimonGMT results that need only locally bounded first variation (Steps 0.5 and 3.1), so no sibling theorem is used. Implementation note: the SimonGMT modules cited below (Chapter08/StationaryCutoff.lean, WeightedRadialIdentity.lean, RadialCutoffDifferentiation.lean, RadialFirstVariation.lean, FirstVariationRiesz.lean, Chapter04/FirstVariation.lean) are all imported by Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.StationaryMonotonicity, which the frozen contract does not import; an implementation file may import it.

Notation. Fix N, n, U, V, x, ρ0, Λ as in the statement and hV : V.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation; the hypothesis (3.1) reads ‖δV‖(B_ρ) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·μ(B_ρ) for 0 < ρ < ρ0. U is open (V.isOpen_domain). μ := V.weight, so μ(A) = V(A × G) for Borel A (Varifold.weight_apply); ‖δV‖ := variationMeasure V; G := G(N,n) = Grassmannian N n; p_S := Grassmannian.project S and p_{S⊥}(v) := v − p_S(v) (orthogonal projections onto S and S⊥); B_s := closedBall x s; ω_n := unitBallVolume n; for t ∈ (0, ρ0), m_t := μ(B_t).toReal = V.weight.real(B_t) (a finite real number, see 0.1). For (y,S) ∈ ℝ^N × G put g(y,S) := |p_{S⊥}(|y − x|^{-1}(y − x))|², with 0^{-1} = 0 so that g(x,S) = 0; since p_{S⊥} is an orthogonal projection, 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 (in SimonGMT g(y,S) = S.radialNormalSq x y, Chapter08/RadialFirstVariation.lean:109, with radialNormalSq_nonneg, radialNormalSq_le_one and measurable_radialNormalSq). All functions below are Borel measurable.

Step 0 (preliminaries).
0.1 For 0 < s < ρ0, B_s ⊆ ball x ρ0 ⊆ U and B_s is compact, so V(B_s × G) = μ(B_s) < ∞ (V.finite_on_compact, Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact).
0.2 0 < ω_n < ∞: ω_n is the volume of the open unit ball of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), a nonempty, open, bounded set, and volume is an additive Haar measure (measure_ball_pos, measure_ball_lt_top; for n = 0, ω_0 = 1).
0.3 For t > 0 and any measure m on ℝ^N: m(B_t)/(ω_n·ofReal(t)^n) = ω_n^{-1}·(m(B_t)/ofReal(t)^n) in [0,∞] (ENNReal.mul_inv, using ω_n ≠ 0, ∞), and ofReal(t)^n = ofReal(t^n) (ENNReal.ofReal_pow). In particular densityRatio n μ x t = ω_n^{-1}·(μ(B_t)/ofReal(t)^n), and the contract's expression ofReal(e^{Λt})·μ(B_t)/ofReal(t)^n equals ofReal(e^{Λt})·(μ(B_t)/ofReal(t)^n) (mul_div_assoc).
0.4 Integrand identity: for every (y,S), |p_{S⊥}(y − x)|²/|y − x|^{n+2} = g(y,S)/|y − x|^n. If y ≠ x, linearity gives p_{S⊥}(y − x) = |y − x|·p_{S⊥}(|y − x|^{-1}(y − x)), so |p_{S⊥}(y − x)|² = |y − x|²·g(y,S) (Grassmannian.normalProject_eq_sub and Grassmannian.norm_normalProject_radial_sq, RadialFirstVariation.lean:81,123); divide by |y − x|^{n+2} > 0. If y = x both sides are 0 (Lean's 0/0 = 0, and g(x,S) = 0). Hence normalDefect V x A = ∫_{A×G} ofReal(g(y,S)/|y − x|^n) dV(y,S) for every set A.
0.5 Since V has locally bounded first variation, ‖δV‖ = variationMeasure V = V.firstVariationRieszMeasure hV (definition of variationMeasure, dif_pos hV). By (3.1) and 0.1, ‖δV‖(B_s) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·μ(B_s) < ∞ for 0 < s < ρ0.

Step 1 (cutoffs and radial test fields). For ε > 0 let φ_ε := monotonicityCutoff ε, φ_ε(τ) = 1 − smoothTransition((τ − 1)/ε) (SimonGMT Chapter04/FirstVariation.lean:825). It is C¹ (contDiff_monotonicityCutoff), antitone, so φ_ε' ≤ 0 (monotonicityCutoff_antitone), has values in [0,1] (monotonicityCutoff_mem_Icc), equals 1 on (−∞,1] and 0 on [1+ε, ∞) (monotonicityCutoff_one, monotonicityCutoff_zero), hence vanishes on [(1+ε)², ∞) (monotonicityCutoff_cutoff). For t > 0 put
   c_t(y) := φ_ε(|y − x|²/t²) ∈ [0,1],   ċ_t(y) := ∂_t c_t(y) = (−2|y − x|²/t³)·φ_ε'(|y − x|²/t²) ≥ 0,   X_t(y) := c_t(y)·(y − x)
(SimonGMT scaledRadialCutoff x φ_ε t, scaledRadialCutoffDeriv x φ_ε t, weightedRadialVectorField x (fun _ ↦ 1) φ_ε t; the t-derivative is hasDerivAt_scaledRadialCutoff, the sign is scaledRadialCutoffDeriv_nonneg). This is Simon's field γ(r)(y − x) with the C¹ profile γ(r) = φ(r/t), φ(s) := φ_ε(s²), which equals 1 on [0,1], vanishes for s ≥ √(1+ε) and is non-increasing on [0,∞). (c_t, ċ_t, X_t and I, J, G below depend on ε; the dependence is suppressed until Step 5.)
1.1 If c_t(y) ≠ 0 then |y − x|²/t² < 1 + ε, so |y − x| < √(1+ε)·t ≤ (1+ε)·t. Hence |X_t(y)| = c_t(y)|y − x| ≤ (1+ε)t·c_t(y) for all y, and tsupport X_t ⊆ B_{(1+ε)t} (weightedRadialVectorField_support with A = 1 + ε).
1.2 If ċ_t(y) ≠ 0 then t ≤ |y − x| ≤ (1+ε)t, because φ_ε is locally constant on (−∞,1) and on ((1+ε)², ∞), so φ_ε' vanishes there (scaledRadialCutoffDeriv_support).
1.3 X_t is C¹ on ℝ^N (contDiff_weightedRadialVectorField) with compact support; if (1+ε)t < ρ0 then tsupport X_t ⊆ B_{(1+ε)t} ⊆ ball x ρ0 ⊆ U, so X_t is a test field in K(U;ℝ^N), i.e. a Varifold.TestVectorField U with toFun = X_t.

Step 2 (the radial identity (★), Simon 3.2). Fix ε > 0 and R ∈ (0, ρ0), so B_R ⊆ U and V(B_R × G) < ∞ (0.1), and let t > 0 with (1+ε)t < R. Put I(t) := ∫ c_t(y) dV(y,S) = ∫ c_t dμ and J(t) := ∫ c_t(y)·g(y,S) dV(y,S).
2.1 (Differentiation under the integral.) For every measurable q on ℝ^N × G with |q| ≤ B on B_R × G, the function t' ↦ ∫ c_{t'}(y) q(y,S) dV is differentiable at t with derivative ∫ ċ_t q dV, and ċ_t q is V-integrable. Reason: choose 0 < t1 < t < t2 with (1+ε)t2 < R; for t' ∈ [t1,t2], c_{t'} and ċ_{t'} vanish off B_R (Steps 1.1–1.2), (t', y) ↦ ċ_{t'}(y) is continuous on [t1,t2] × B_R and hence bounded by some C, so |ċ_{t'} q| ≤ C·B·1_{B_R×G}, which is V-integrable; dominated differentiation applies (SimonGMT Varifold.hasDerivAt_integral_radialCutoff_of_radius, Chapter08/RadialCutoffDifferentiation.lean:91, with A = 1 + ε). In particular I'(t) = ∫ ċ_t dV and J'(t) = ∫ ċ_t g dV.
2.2 (Pointwise divergence.) For all (y,S): div_S X_t(y) = n·c_t(y) − t·ċ_t(y) + t·ċ_t(y)·g(y,S). Indeed, with η(τ) := φ_ε(τ/t²), X_t(y) = η(|y − x|²)(y − x) and DX_t(y) = η(|y − x|²)·Id + 2η'(|y − x|²)·(y − x)⊗(y − x), so div_S X_t(y) = trace(p_S DX_t(y)) = n·η + 2η'(|y − x|²)·|p_S(y − x)|²; moreover |p_S(y − x)|² = |y − x|² − |p_{S⊥}(y − x)|² = |y − x|²(1 − g(y,S)) by 0.4, and 2η'(|y − x|²)|y − x|² = 2|y − x|²φ_ε'(|y − x|²/t²)/t² = −t·ċ_t(y). (SimonGMT tangentialDivergence_weightedRadialVectorField, Chapter08/WeightedRadialIdentity.lean:44, with h ≡ 1, whose gradient term vanishes.)
2.3 Integrating 2.2 against V (every term is integrable by 2.1 and 0.1) gives δV(X_t) = n·I(t) − t·I'(t) + t·J'(t) (SimonGMT weightedRadial_firstVariation_identity, WeightedRadialIdentity.lean:152, with h ≡ 1).
2.4 Therefore t' ↦ I(t')/t'^n is differentiable at t and
   (I/t^n)'(t) = I'(t)/t^n − n·I(t)/t^{n+1} = J'(t)/t^n − δV(X_t)/t^{n+1}.        (★)
(SimonGMT Varifold.hasDerivAt_normalized_weightedCutoffMass, WeightedRadialIdentity.lean:200, with h ≡ 1, where the gradient integral is 0 and deriv J(t) = ∫ ċ_t g dV by hasDerivAt_weightedCutoffNormalMass, line 96; here I = weightedCutoffMass x (fun _ ↦ 1) φ_ε and J = weightedCutoffNormalMass x (fun _ ↦ 1) φ_ε.)
2.5 J'(t) = ∫ ċ_t g dV ≥ 0, because ċ_t ≥ 0 and g ≥ 0.

Step 3 (bound for the first variation). Let ε > 0 and t > 0 with (1+ε)t < ρ0. Then |δV(X_t)| ≤ (1+ε)·Λ·t·I(t).
3.1 (Polar representation, Simon 2.6.) By SimonGMT Varifold.isFirstVariationPolarRepresentation_riesz (Chapter08/FirstVariationRiesz.lean:133; it needs only locally bounded first variation) and 0.5, there is a measurable ν : ℝ^N → ℝ^N with |ν| = 1 ‖δV‖-a.e. such that for every test field X ∈ K(U;ℝ^N), y ↦ ⟨ν(y), X(y)⟩ is ‖δV‖-integrable and δV(X) = −∫⟨ν, X⟩ d‖δV‖. Apply this to X_t (Step 1.3). By Cauchy–Schwarz and Step 1.1, |δV(X_t)| ≤ ∫|⟨ν, X_t⟩| d‖δV‖ ≤ ∫|X_t| d‖δV‖ ≤ (1+ε)t·∫ c_t d‖δV‖; all these integrals are finite because c_t ≤ 1_{B_{(1+ε)t}} and ‖δV‖(B_{(1+ε)t}) < ∞ (0.5).
3.2 (Layer cake with closed super-level sets.) For any measure m on ℝ^N, since c_t is continuous with 0 ≤ c_t ≤ 1, ∫⁻ ofReal(c_t) dm = ∫⁻_{s ∈ (0,∞)} m({c_t ≥ s}) ds (Mathlib MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le, MeasureTheory/Integral/Layercake.lean:445), and {c_t ≥ s} = ∅ for s > 1.
3.3 For s ∈ (0,1] the set {c_t ≥ s} is a closed ball B_r with 0 < r < ρ0. Indeed E := {τ ∈ ℝ : φ_ε(τ) ≥ s} is closed (φ_ε is continuous), down-closed (φ_ε is antitone), contains (−∞,1] (φ_ε = 1 ≥ s there) and is disjoint from [1+ε, ∞) (φ_ε = 0 < s there); hence b := sup E belongs to E, 1 ≤ b < 1 + ε, and E = (−∞, b]. Thus {c_t ≥ s} = {y : |y − x|²/t² ≤ b} = B_r with r := t√b, and t ≤ r < √(1+ε)·t ≤ (1+ε)t < ρ0. By (3.1), ‖δV‖({c_t ≥ s}) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·μ({c_t ≥ s}).
3.4 Hence ∫⁻ ofReal(c_t) d‖δV‖ = ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ‖δV‖({c_t ≥ s}) ds ≤ ofReal(Λ)·∫⁻_{(0,∞)} μ({c_t ≥ s}) ds = ofReal(Λ)·∫⁻ ofReal(c_t) dμ. Both lintegrals are finite (c_t ≤ 1_{B_{(1+ε)t}}, 0.1, 0.5), so taking toReal gives ∫ c_t d‖δV‖ ≤ Λ·∫ c_t dμ = Λ·I(t), and with 3.1, |δV(X_t)| ≤ (1+ε)·Λ·t·I(t).

Step 4 (integrating factor and comparison, Ch. 4 3.5). Fix 0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0, put R := (ρ + ρ0)/2 ∈ (ρ, ρ0), and consider ε > 0 with (1+ε)ρ < R (all sufficiently small ε > 0 qualify). Write Λ_ε := (1+ε)Λ ≥ 0. For every t ∈ [σ, ρ], (1+ε)t ≤ (1+ε)ρ < R < ρ0, so Steps 2 and 3 apply at t (with this R).
4.1 F(t) := e^{Λ_ε t}·I(t)/t^n is differentiable at each t ∈ [σ, ρ] with F'(t) = e^{Λ_ε t}·[Λ_ε I(t)/t^n + J'(t)/t^n − δV(X_t)/t^{n+1}] (product rule and (★)). Since δV(X_t) ≤ Λ_ε·t·I(t) (Step 3), the bracket is ≥ J'(t)/t^n; since J'(t) ≥ 0 (2.5) and e^{Λ_ε t} ≥ 1 (Λ_ε t ≥ 0), F'(t) ≥ J'(t)/t^n.
4.2 Let q(y,S) := g(y,S)/max(σ, |y − x|)^n (SimonGMT truncatedRadialDefect x σ, Chapter08/StationaryCutoff.lean:121), a measurable function with 0 ≤ q ≤ σ^{-n} (norm_truncatedRadialDefect_le), and G(t) := ∫ c_t q dV. By 2.1, G is differentiable at every t ∈ [σ, ρ] with G'(t) = ∫ ċ_t q dV. Pointwise ċ_t q ≤ ċ_t g/t^n: where ċ_t(y) ≠ 0, Step 1.2 gives |y − x| ≥ t ≥ σ, so q = g/|y − x|^n ≤ g/t^n, and ċ_t ≥ 0; where ċ_t(y) = 0 both sides vanish (SimonGMT Varifold.scaledRadialCutoffDeriv_defect_bounds, StationaryCutoff.lean:142, first half). Integrating, G'(t) ≤ J'(t)/t^n ≤ F'(t).
4.3 F − G is differentiable at every point of [σ, ρ], hence continuous there, with nonnegative derivative, so it is non-decreasing on [σ, ρ] (mean value theorem; Mathlib monotoneOn_of_deriv_nonneg on Icc σ ρ). Writing the dependence on ε explicitly:
   e^{Λ_ε ρ}·I_ε(ρ)/ρ^n − e^{Λ_ε σ}·I_ε(σ)/σ^n ≥ G_ε(ρ) − G_ε(σ).        (4.3)

Step 5 (ε ↓ 0). Keep σ, ρ, R fixed; (4.3) holds for all sufficiently small ε > 0. As ε → 0+:
5.1 For t ∈ {σ, ρ} and every y, c_t(y) = φ_ε(|y − x|²/t²) → 1_{B_t}(y): if |y − x| ≤ t it equals 1 for every ε; if |y − x| > t it equals 0 as soon as 1 + ε ≤ |y − x|²/t² (SimonGMT tendsto_scaledRadialCutoff, Chapter04/FirstVariation.lean:886). For ε with (1+ε)t < R, |c_t| ≤ 1_{B_R×G} and |c_t q| ≤ σ^{-n}·1_{B_R×G}, both V-integrable (0.1). By dominated convergence I_ε(t) → m_t = V.weight.real(B_t) and G_ε(t) → ∫_{B_t×G} q dV (SimonGMT Varifold.tendsto_cutoffMass and Varifold.tendsto_integral_radialCutoff, StationaryCutoff.lean:111 and 63, with this R).
5.2 e^{Λ_ε t} = e^{(1+ε)Λt} → e^{Λt}.
5.3 Passing to the limit in (4.3), an inequality between real numbers:
   e^{Λρ}m_ρ/ρ^n − e^{Λσ}m_σ/σ^n ≥ ∫_{B_ρ×G} q dV − ∫_{B_σ×G} q dV = ∫_{(B_ρ∖B_σ)×G} q dV = ∫_{(B_ρ∖B_σ)×G} g(y,S)/|y − x|^n dV(y,S),
because q is V-integrable on B_ρ × G, B_σ × G ⊆ B_ρ × G, (B_ρ × G) ∖ (B_σ × G) = (B_ρ ∖ B_σ) × G, and on that annulus |y − x| > σ, so max(σ, |y − x|) = |y − x|.

Step 6 (additive form of 3.3 and normalisation). Let D := normalDefect V x (B_ρ ∖ B_σ). By 0.4, D = ∫_{(B_ρ∖B_σ)×G} ofReal(g/|y − x|^n) dV = ofReal(∫_{(B_ρ∖B_σ)×G} g/|y − x|^n dV), the integrand being nonnegative and V-integrable (bounded by σ^{-n} on a set of finite V-measure; ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal). Write 5.3 as a + d ≤ b with a := e^{Λσ}m_σ/σ^n ≥ 0, d := ∫_{(B_ρ∖B_σ)×G} g/|y − x|^n dV ≥ 0 and b := e^{Λρ}m_ρ/ρ^n; apply ofReal (monotone, and additive on nonnegative reals) and use ofReal(e^{Λt}·m_t/t^n) = ofReal(e^{Λt})·ofReal(m_t)/ofReal(t)^n (ofReal_mul, ofReal_div_of_pos, ofReal_pow) together with ofReal(m_t) = μ(B_t) (ofReal_toReal, μ(B_t) finite by 0.1). This gives
   ofReal(e^{Λσ})·μ(B_σ)/ofReal(σ)^n + D ≤ ofReal(e^{Λρ})·μ(B_ρ)/ofReal(ρ)^n.        (3.3)
Multiplying (3.3) by the finite constant ω_n^{-1} and using 0.3 and distributivity:
   ofReal(e^{Λσ})·densityRatio n μ x σ + ω_n^{-1}·normalDefect V x (B_ρ ∖ B_σ) ≤ ofReal(e^{Λρ})·densityRatio n μ x ρ
for all 0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0 — the second inequality of the conclusion.

Step 7 (monotonicity). Let f(t) := ofReal(e^{Λt})·μ(B_t)/ofReal(t)^n. For σ, ρ ∈ (0, ρ0) with σ ≤ ρ, (3.3) and D ≥ 0 give f(σ) ≤ f(σ) + D ≤ f(ρ). Hence f is MonotoneOn (Ioo 0 ρ0); f is exactly the function in the contract (0.3).

Step 8 (the density θ). Let h(t) := ofReal(e^{Λt})·densityRatio n μ x t = ω_n^{-1}·f(t) (0.3). By Step 7, h is monotone on (0, ρ0) and bounded below by 0, so h(t) → θ := inf{h(s) : s ∈ (0, ρ0)} as t → 0+ (Mathlib MonotoneOn.tendsto_nhdsWithin_Ioo_right, Topology/Order/Monotone.lean:457). For t > 0, ofReal(e^{−Λt})·ofReal(e^{Λt}) = ofReal(1) = 1, so densityRatio n μ x t = ofReal(e^{−Λt})·h(t); as t → 0+, ofReal(e^{−Λt}) → 1, and multiplication on [0,∞] is continuous at (1, θ) because 1 ≠ 0 and 1 ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.Tendsto.mul), so densityRatio n μ x t → θ, i.e. HasDensity n μ x θ. For every σ ∈ (0, ρ0), θ ≤ h(σ) = ofReal(e^{Λσ})·densityRatio n μ x σ (θ is the infimum) — the first inequality of the conclusion. Finally θ ≤ h(ρ0/2) = ofReal(e^{Λρ0/2})·μ(B_{ρ0/2})/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ0/2)^n) < ∞ by 0.1–0.2, so θ ≠ ∞.

Step 9 (conclusion). Steps 6–8 give the monotonicity of f on (0, ρ0) and a θ with HasDensity n μ x θ, θ ≠ ∞, and both inequalities for all 0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0. Since N, n, U, V, x, ρ0, Λ were arbitrary, MonotonicityFormula holds. Nothing above uses n ≥ 1: for n = 0, t^0 = 1, ω_0 = 1 and the defect integrand equals g = 1 off y = x.
proof_key_steps: Preliminaries: μ_V(B_s(x)) < ∞ for 0 < s < ρ0; 0 < ω_n < ∞; densityRatio = ω_n^{-1}·μ_V(B_t)/ofReal(t)^n; the integrand identity |p_{S⊥}(y−x)|²/r^{n+2} = g/r^n with g = |p_{S⊥}((y−x)/r)|² (both 0 at y = x); ‖δV‖ = variationMeasure V = firstVariationRieszMeasure (dif_pos).
Radial cutoff fields X_t(y) = φ_ε(|y−x|²/t²)(y−x) (φ_ε = monotonicityCutoff ε) are test fields when (1+ε)t < ρ0, with |X_t| ≤ (1+ε)t·c_t and ∂_t c_t supported in t ≤ r ≤ (1+ε)t.
Radial identity (★): d/dt(I/t^n) = J'/t^n − δV(X_t)/t^{n+1} with I = ∫c_t dμ_V, J = ∫c_t g dV and J' ≥ 0 (SimonGMT hasDerivAt_normalized_weightedCutoffMass with h ≡ 1).

Polar representation (SimonGMT isFirstVariationPolarRepresentation_riesz) gives |δV(X_t)| ≤ (1+ε)t∫c_t d‖δV‖; the layer cake over the closed super-level sets {c_t ≥ s} = B_r(x), r < ρ0, and the hypothesis give ∫c_t d‖δV‖ ≤ Λ I(t).
Integrating factor: F = e^{Λ_ε t}I/t^n has F' ≥ J'/t^n ≥ G' with G = ∫c_t·g/max(σ,r)^n dV; the mean value theorem on [σ,ρ] gives F(ρ) − F(σ) ≥ G(ρ) − G(σ).
Let ε ↓ 0 by dominated convergence: e^{Λρ}μ_V(B_ρ)/ρ^n − e^{Λσ}μ_V(B_σ)/σ^n ≥ ∫_{(B_ρ∖B_σ)×G} g/r^n dV.

Pass to [0,∞] (all terms finite), identify the defect with normalDefect, multiply by ω_n^{-1}: the defect inequality; dropping the defect gives monotonicity of ofReal(e^{Λρ})μ_V(B_ρ)/ofReal(ρ)^n on (0,ρ0).
θ := inf over (0,ρ0) of ofReal(e^{Λt})·densityRatio(t) is its limit at 0+; since ofReal(e^{−Λt}) → 1, HasDensity n μ_V x θ; θ ≤ ofReal(e^{Λσ})·densityRatio(σ) and θ ≠ ∞.

subproblems.title: Stationary monotonicity identity (Simon 8.3.4)
subproblems.statement: (Simon Ch. 8, 3.4; exactly the contract Prop StationaryMonotonicityIdentity.) For all N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N, every n-varifold V on U (no first-variation hypothesis), x ∈ ℝ^N and ρ0 > 0 with ball x ρ0 ⊆ U: if V.firstVariation X = 0 for every test field X ∈ K(U;ℝ^N) (Varifold.TestVectorField U) with tsupport X ⊆ ball x ρ0, then there is θ ∈ [0,∞] with HasDensity n μ_V x θ such that θ + ω_n^{-1}·normalDefect V x (B_ρ(x)) = densityRatio n μ_V x ρ for every 0 < ρ < ρ0, where B_ρ(x) = closedBall x ρ, μ_V = V.weight, ω_n = unitBallVolume n, densityRatio n μ x ρ = μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ)^n), and normalDefect V x A = ∫_{A×G(N,n)} ofReal(|(y − x) − p_S(y − x)|²/|y − x|^{n+2}) dV(y,S) (integrand 0 at y = x by Lean's 0/0 = 0).
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory, Ch. 8, 3.4 (printed p. 211): the Λ = 0 case of 3.3, obtained “by essentially the same computation as in §4 of Ch. 4” (Ch. 4, 3.1–3.6) with the radial test field X_y = γ(r)(y − x). The argument below is extracted from the parent node's accepted proof (its common radial computation and its Part B) with all details filled in; it is self-contained. Errata/normalisations: (i) 3.4 needs no locally-bounded-first-variation hypothesis, only stationarity in B°_{ρ0}(x); (ii) the printed subtraction is written additively in [0,∞], which is equivalent because all terms are finite. Implementation note: the SimonGMT modules cited below (Chapter08/StationaryMonotonicity.lean, StationaryCutoff.lean, WeightedRadialIdentity.lean, RadialCutoffDifferentiation.lean, RadialFirstVariation.lean, Chapter04/FirstVariation.lean) are all imported by Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.StationaryMonotonicity, which the frozen contract does not import; an implementation file may import it.

Notation. Fix N, n, U, V, x, ρ0 as in the statement, with the stationarity hypothesis (H): V.firstVariation X = 0 for every test field X ∈ K(U;ℝ^N) (Varifold.TestVectorField U) with tsupport X ⊆ ball x ρ0. U is open (V.isOpen_domain). μ := V.weight (μ(A) = V(A × G) for Borel A); G := G(N,n) = Grassmannian N n; p_S := Grassmannian.project S and p_{S⊥}(v) := v − p_S(v); B_s := closedBall x s; B°_s := ball x s; ω_n := unitBallVolume n. For (y,S) put g(y,S) := |p_{S⊥}(|y − x|^{-1}(y − x))|² ∈ [0,1], with 0^{-1} = 0 so that g(x,S) = 0 (SimonGMT S.radialNormalSq x y, Chapter08/RadialFirstVariation.lean:109). For t > 0 put P(t) := μ(B_t)/ofReal(t^n) (SimonGMT Varifold.normalizedBallMass V x t, StationaryMonotonicity.lean:111), and let f(y,S) := ofReal(|p_{S⊥}(y − x)|²/|y − x|^{n+2}) be the integrand of normalDefect V x, so normalDefect V x A = ∫_{A×G} f dV.

Step 0 (preliminaries).
0.1 For 0 < s < ρ0, B_s ⊆ B°_{ρ0} ⊆ U and B_s is compact, so V(B_s × G) = μ(B_s) < ∞ (V.finite_on_compact) and P(s) < ∞.
0.2 0 < ω_n < ∞ (the open unit ball of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is nonempty, open and bounded, and volume is an additive Haar measure: measure_ball_pos, measure_ball_lt_top; ω_0 = 1). For t > 0, ofReal(t)^n = ofReal(t^n) (ENNReal.ofReal_pow) and densityRatio n μ x t = μ(B_t)/(ω_n·ofReal(t)^n) = ω_n^{-1}·P(t) (ENNReal.mul_inv, using ω_n ≠ 0, ∞).
0.3 For every (y,S): |p_{S⊥}(y − x)|²/|y − x|^{n+2} = g(y,S)/|y − x|^n. For y ≠ x, homogeneity gives |p_{S⊥}(y − x)|² = |y − x|²·g(y,S) (Grassmannian.normalProject_eq_sub and Grassmannian.norm_normalProject_radial_sq, RadialFirstVariation.lean:81,123); for y = x both sides are 0 (Lean's 0/0 = 0, g(x,S) = 0). Hence f(y,S) = ofReal(g(y,S)/|y − x|^n), f(x,S) = 0, and normalDefect V x A = ∫_{A×G} ofReal(g/|y − x|^n) dV for every set A; in particular normalDefect V x (B_ρ ∖ B_σ) equals SimonGMT's Varifold.annularMonotonicityDefect V x σ ρ (StationaryMonotonicity.lean:120).
0.4 For 0 < R < ρ0: B_R ⊆ B°_{ρ0} ⊆ U, and every test field X with tsupport X ⊆ B°_R also has tsupport X ⊆ B°_{ρ0}, so δV(X) = 0 by (H); that is, V is StationaryOn (ball x R) in the sense of SimonGMT (Chapter08/StationaryCutoff.lean:28).

Step 1 (the annular identity). For 0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0:
   P(σ) + normalDefect V x (B_ρ ∖ B_σ) = P(ρ).        (1)
Let R := (ρ + ρ0)/2 ∈ (ρ, ρ0); by 0.1 and 0.4, B_R ⊆ U, V(B_R × G) < ∞, and δV vanishes on test fields supported in B°_R. (Formal shortcut: (1) is SimonGMT Varifold.StationaryOn.stationaryMonotonicity, StationaryMonotonicity.lean:131, applied with this R, after rewriting normalizedBallMass and annularMonotonicityDefect by 0.2–0.3; its proof is the following computation.)
1.1 Cutoffs and fields. For ε > 0 let φ_ε := monotonicityCutoff ε (SimonGMT Chapter04/FirstVariation.lean:825): C¹, antitone (so φ_ε' ≤ 0), with values in [0,1], equal to 1 on (−∞,1] and to 0 on [1+ε, ∞). For t > 0 let c_t(y) := φ_ε(|y − x|²/t²) ∈ [0,1], ċ_t(y) := ∂_t c_t(y) = (−2|y − x|²/t³)·φ_ε'(|y − x|²/t²) ≥ 0, and X_t(y) := c_t(y)·(y − x) (SimonGMT scaledRadialCutoff, scaledRadialCutoffDeriv, weightedRadialVectorField x (fun _ ↦ 1) φ_ε t). If c_t(y) ≠ 0 then |y − x| < √(1+ε)·t ≤ (1+ε)t, so tsupport X_t ⊆ B_{(1+ε)t} (weightedRadialVectorField_support); if ċ_t(y) ≠ 0 then t ≤ |y − x| ≤ (1+ε)t, since φ_ε is locally constant on (−∞,1) and on ((1+ε)², ∞) (scaledRadialCutoffDeriv_support); X_t is C¹ with compact support (contDiff_weightedRadialVectorField); ċ_t ≥ 0 (scaledRadialCutoffDeriv_nonneg). (All objects depend on ε; the dependence is suppressed until 1.6.)
1.2 Fix ε > 0 with (1+ε)ρ < R and let t ∈ [σ, ρ]; then (1+ε)t < R. Put I(t) := ∫ c_t dV = ∫ c_t dμ, J(t) := ∫ c_t g dV, q(y,S) := g(y,S)/max(σ, |y − x|)^n ∈ [0, σ^{-n}] (SimonGMT truncatedRadialDefect x σ, StationaryCutoff.lean:121) and G(t) := ∫ c_t q dV. Differentiation under the integral sign: for t' in a compact neighbourhood [t1,t2] of t with t1 > 0 and (1+ε)t2 < R, the integrands and their t'-derivatives vanish off B_R × G and are bounded there by a constant (ċ_{t'}(y) is jointly continuous in (t',y)), and V(B_R × G) < ∞; hence I'(t) = ∫ ċ_t dV, J'(t) = ∫ ċ_t g dV and G'(t) = ∫ ċ_t q dV, all integrands being V-integrable (SimonGMT Varifold.hasDerivAt_integral_radialCutoff_of_radius, RadialCutoffDifferentiation.lean:91, with A = 1 + ε).
1.3 The radial identity. For all (y,S), div_S X_t(y) = n·c_t(y) − t·ċ_t(y) + t·ċ_t(y)·g(y,S): with η(τ) := φ_ε(τ/t²), DX_t = η(|y − x|²)·Id + 2η'(|y − x|²)·(y − x)⊗(y − x), trace(p_S DX_t) = n·η + 2η'·|p_S(y − x)|², |p_S(y − x)|² = |y − x|²(1 − g) by 0.3, and 2η'(|y − x|²)|y − x|² = −t·ċ_t(y) (SimonGMT tangentialDivergence_weightedRadialVectorField, WeightedRadialIdentity.lean:44, with h ≡ 1). Integrating against V gives δV(X_t) = n·I(t) − t·I'(t) + t·J'(t), hence (I/t^n)'(t) = I'(t)/t^n − n·I(t)/t^{n+1} = J'(t)/t^n − δV(X_t)/t^{n+1} (SimonGMT hasDerivAt_normalized_weightedCutoffMass, WeightedRadialIdentity.lean:200, h ≡ 1). Since tsupport X_t ⊆ B_{(1+ε)t} ⊆ B°_R ⊆ U, X_t is a test field in K(U;ℝ^N) supported in B°_R, so δV(X_t) = 0 by 0.4, and therefore
   (I/t^n)'(t) = J'(t)/t^n        (SimonGMT StationaryOn.hasDerivAt_normalizedCutoffMass, StationaryCutoff.lean:39).
1.4 Two-sided comparison. Pointwise ċ_t q ≤ ċ_t g/t^n ≤ (1+ε)^n·ċ_t q: where ċ_t(y) ≠ 0 we have σ ≤ t ≤ |y − x| ≤ (1+ε)t, so q = g/|y − x|^n and |y − x|^{-n} ≤ t^{-n} ≤ (1+ε)^n·|y − x|^{-n}, while ċ_t, g ≥ 0; where ċ_t(y) = 0 all three vanish (SimonGMT Varifold.scaledRadialCutoffDeriv_defect_bounds, StationaryCutoff.lean:142). Integrating, G'(t) ≤ J'(t)/t^n ≤ (1+ε)^n·G'(t).
1.5 Integration over [σ, ρ]. The functions t ↦ I(t)/t^n and t ↦ G(t) are differentiable at every t ∈ [σ, ρ]. By 1.3–1.4, t ↦ I(t)/t^n − G(t) and t ↦ (1+ε)^n G(t) − I(t)/t^n have nonnegative derivatives on [σ, ρ], so by the mean value theorem (Mathlib monotoneOn_of_deriv_nonneg on Icc σ ρ) they are non-decreasing there, i.e.
   G_ε(ρ) − G_ε(σ) ≤ I_ε(ρ)/ρ^n − I_ε(σ)/σ^n ≤ (1+ε)^n·(G_ε(ρ) − G_ε(σ))
(SimonGMT StationaryOn.cutoff_squeeze, StationaryCutoff.lean:188).
1.6 ε ↓ 0. For t ∈ {σ, ρ}, c_t → 1_{B_t} pointwise as ε → 0+ (if |y − x| ≤ t it is 1 for all ε; if |y − x| > t it is 0 once 1 + ε ≤ |y − x|²/t²), with |c_t| ≤ 1_{B_R×G} and |c_t q| ≤ σ^{-n}·1_{B_R×G} once (1+ε)t < R; by dominated convergence I_ε(t) → μ(B_t) and G_ε(t) → ∫_{B_t×G} q dV (SimonGMT Varifold.tendsto_cutoffMass and Varifold.tendsto_integral_radialCutoff, StationaryCutoff.lean:111 and 63), and (1+ε)^n → 1. The squeeze in 1.5 yields the real identity
   μ(B_ρ)/ρ^n − μ(B_σ)/σ^n = ∫_{B_ρ×G} q dV − ∫_{B_σ×G} q dV = ∫_{(B_ρ∖B_σ)×G} g(y,S)/|y − x|^n dV(y,S),
because q is V-integrable on B_ρ × G, B_σ × G ⊆ B_ρ × G, and on the annulus |y − x| > σ, so q = g/|y − x|^n there (SimonGMT StationaryOn.stationaryMonotonicity_real, StationaryMonotonicity.lean:52).
1.7 The right-hand side is ≥ 0 and all terms are finite (0.1), so applying ofReal (additive on nonnegative reals) gives P(σ) + ∫_{(B_ρ∖B_σ)×G} ofReal(g/|y − x|^n) dV = P(ρ): indeed ofReal(μ(B_t).toReal/t^n) = μ(B_t)/ofReal(t^n) = P(t) (ofReal_div_of_pos, ofReal_toReal), and the Bochner integral of the nonnegative V-integrable function g/|y − x|^n over the annulus equals the toReal of its lintegral (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal). By 0.3 that lintegral is normalDefect V x (B_ρ ∖ B_σ), which proves (1).

Step 2 (existence of the density). By (1) and normalDefect ≥ 0, P(σ) ≤ P(ρ) whenever 0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0, i.e. P is monotone on (0, ρ0). Hence P(t) → L := inf{P(s) : s ∈ (0, ρ0)} as t → 0+ (Mathlib MonotoneOn.tendsto_nhdsWithin_Ioo_right, Topology/Order/Monotone.lean:457; alternatively SimonGMT StationaryOn.tendsto_normalizedBallMass_atRight with any R ∈ (0, ρ0), StationaryMonotonicity.lean:174), and L ≤ P(ρ0/2) < ∞. Put θ := ω_n^{-1}·L. For t > 0, densityRatio n μ x t = ω_n^{-1}·P(t) (0.2), and multiplication by the finite constant ω_n^{-1} is continuous on [0,∞] (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul), so densityRatio n μ x t → ω_n^{-1}·L = θ as t → 0+, i.e. HasDensity n μ x θ.

Step 3 (σ ↓ 0). Fix ρ ∈ (0, ρ0). For k ∈ ℕ let σ_k := ρ/(k+1) ∈ (0, ρ] and A_k := B_ρ ∖ B_{σ_k}.
3.1 (A_k) is increasing (σ_k decreases), and ⋃_k A_k = B_ρ ∖ {x}: x ∉ A_k for every k, and if y ∈ B_ρ, y ≠ x, then |y − x| > σ_k for all large k.
3.2 For measurable A, normalDefect V x A = ∫_{A×G} f dV = (V.measure.withDensity f)(A × G) (MeasureTheory.withDensity_apply). The measurable sets A_k × G increase to (B_ρ ∖ {x}) × G, so by continuity from below (MeasureTheory.tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop) normalDefect V x A_k → normalDefect V x (B_ρ ∖ {x}) as k → ∞.
3.3 normalDefect V x (B_ρ ∖ {x}) = normalDefect V x (B_ρ): B_ρ × G is the disjoint union of the measurable sets (B_ρ ∖ {x}) × G and {x} × G, and on {x} × G the integrand is f(x,S) = ofReal(|0 − p_S(0)|²/|0|^{n+2}) = ofReal(0/0) = 0, so the second piece contributes 0.
3.4 By (1), P(σ_k) + normalDefect V x A_k = P(ρ) for every k. As k → ∞, σ_k → 0 with σ_k > 0, so P(σ_k) → L by Step 2, and normalDefect V x A_k → normalDefect V x (B_ρ) by 3.2–3.3. Addition on [0,∞] is continuous, so the constant sequence P(ρ) converges to L + normalDefect V x (B_ρ); by uniqueness of limits, L + normalDefect V x (B_ρ) = P(ρ).
3.5 Multiplying by ω_n^{-1} and using left distributivity and 0.2: θ + ω_n^{-1}·normalDefect V x (B_ρ) = ω_n^{-1}·P(ρ) = densityRatio n μ x ρ.

Step 4 (conclusion). θ satisfies HasDensity n μ x θ (Step 2) and θ + ω_n^{-1}·normalDefect V x (closedBall x ρ) = densityRatio n μ x ρ for every 0 < ρ < ρ0 (Step 3). Since N, n, U, V, x, ρ0 were arbitrary, StationaryMonotonicityIdentity holds. Nothing above uses n ≥ 1 or any first-variation bound (for n = 0 the integrand is 1 off the centre and the identity reads μ({x}) + μ(B_ρ ∖ {x}) = μ(B_ρ)).
proof_key_steps: Preliminaries: μ_V(B_s(x)) < ∞ for s < ρ0; 0 < ω_n < ∞; densityRatio = ω_n^{-1}·P with P(t) = μ_V(B_t)/ofReal(t^n); normalDefect integrand = ofReal(g/r^n) everywhere (0 at y = x), so normalDefect on annuli is SimonGMT annularMonotonicityDefect; V is StationaryOn (ball x R) for every R < ρ0.

Annular identity P(σ) + normalDefect V x (B_ρ∖B_σ) = P(ρ) for 0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0: radial cutoff fields supported in ball x R have δV = 0, so d/dt(I/t^n) = J'/t^n; two-sided cutoff squeeze G' ≤ J'/t^n ≤ (1+ε)^n G'; integrate on [σ,ρ]; ε ↓ 0 (SimonGMT StationaryOn.stationaryMonotonicity with R = (ρ+ρ0)/2).
P is monotone on (0,ρ0), so L = lim_{t↓0} P(t) = inf P exists and is finite; θ := ω_n^{-1}·L satisfies HasDensity n μ_V x θ.

With σ_k = ρ/(k+1): normalDefect V x (B_ρ∖B_{σ_k}) ↑ normalDefect V x (B_ρ∖{x}) = normalDefect V x (B_ρ) (continuity from below; centre integrand 0); pass to the limit in the annular identity and multiply by ω_n^{-1}.

subproblems.title: A.e. existence and Borel measurability of the density (Simon Lemma 8.3.6)
subproblems.statement: (Simon Ch. 8, Lemma 3.6; exactly the contract Prop DensityExistsAE.) For all N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N and every n-varifold V on U with locally bounded first variation in U, there is a Borel measurable Θ : ℝ^N → [0,∞] such that for μ_V-a.e. x: Θ(x) ≠ ∞ and HasDensity n μ_V x (Θ x), i.e. densityRatio n μ_V x ρ = μ_V(closedBall x ρ)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ)^n) → Θ(x) as ρ ↓ 0 (μ_V = V.weight, ω_n = unitBallVolume n).
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory, Ch. 8, Lemma 3.6 and its printed proof (p. 211); the argument below is the parent node's accepted Part C with details filled in; it is self-contained apart from the sibling statement named below. No erratum; one detail is filled in: the printed claim “μ_V(B_ρ(x)) ≥ limsup_{y→x} μ_V(B_ρ(y))”, which needs finiteness of μ_V on a slightly larger ball, is replaced, for the Borel measurability of x ↦ μ_V(B_ρ(x)), by Tonelli's theorem, which holds for every x. The only sibling used is monotonicity_formula, i.e. Submission.monotonicity_formula_8_3_3 : MonotonicityFormula. Notation. Fix N, n, U and V with hV : V.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation. U is open (V.isOpen_domain). μ := V.weight, ‖δV‖ := variationMeasure V, B_t(a) := closedBall a t, ω_n := unitBallVolume n, G := Grassmannian N n.

Step 1 (a.e. ball bound: the parenthetical remark of 3.6). For μ-a.e. x there are R_x > 0 and Λ_x ≥ 0 with B_{R_x}(x) ⊆ U and ‖δV‖(B_r(x)) ≤ ofReal(Λ_x)·μ(B_r(x)) for all 0 < r < R_x.
Proof. SimonGMT Varifold.ae_exists_ballFirstVariationBound_inside (Chapter08/BallVariationBound.lean:66) states exactly this with V.firstVariationRieszMeasure hV in place of ‖δV‖ (in the form V.HasBallFirstVariationBound hV x R Λ, i.e. ∀ r, 0 < r → r < R → V.firstVariationRieszMeasure hV (B_r(x)) ≤ ofReal Λ · μ(B_r(x))), and variationMeasure V = V.firstVariationRieszMeasure hV by the definition of variationMeasure (dif_pos hV). For completeness, its proof: (a) μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = V((ℝ^N ∖ U) × G) = 0 (V.supported); (b) by the differentiation theorem for Radon measures (Besicovitch; Simon Ch. 8, 2.7; SimonGMT firstVariationRiesz_symmetricDensity_spec, FirstVariationRiesz.lean:254), for μ-a.e. x the ratio ‖δV‖(B_r(x))/μ(B_r(x)) converges as r ↓ 0 to a finite D(x) ∈ [0,∞); (c) for such x ∈ U put Λ_x := D(x).toReal + 1 > D(x); then the ratio is < Λ_x for 0 < r < r1 (some r1 > 0), and in [0,∞] a/b < Λ_x < ∞ forces a ≤ Λ_x·b (ENNReal.div_le_iff_le_mul; also when b = 0); (d) U is open, so ball x r2 ⊆ U for some r2 > 0; with R_x := min(r1, r2/2) one has B_{R_x}(x) ⊆ ball x r2 ⊆ U and the bound for 0 < r < R_x.

Step 2 (existence and finiteness: “the first part of the lemma follows directly from the monotonicity formula 3.3”). Let x be as in Step 1. Apply MonotonicityFormula (the sibling Submission.monotonicity_formula_8_3_3) to N, n, U, V, x, ρ0 := R_x and Λ := Λ_x: its hypotheses are hV, 0 < R_x, ball x R_x ⊆ B_{R_x}(x) ⊆ U, 0 ≤ Λ_x, and variationMeasure V (B_r(x)) ≤ ofReal(Λ_x)·μ(B_r(x)) for all 0 < r < R_x (Step 1). The second part of its conclusion gives θ_x ∈ [0,∞] with HasDensity n μ x θ_x and θ_x ≠ ∞. Hence for μ-a.e. x there is θ_x ≠ ∞ with HasDensity n μ x θ_x.

Step 3 (Borel measurability of ball masses). Fix t ∈ ℝ. The set E_t := {(a,b) ∈ ℝ^N × ℝ^N : dist(b,a) ≤ t} is closed (continuity of the distance), hence measurable in ℝ^N × ℝ^N (ℝ^N is second countable, so open, hence closed, subsets of the product are measurable for the product σ-algebra), and {b : (a,b) ∈ E_t} = B_t(a) for every a. μ is σ-finite (SimonGMT instance Varifold.weight.instSigmaFinite, Chapter08/Varifold.lean:615: μ is finite on compact subsets of U and vanishes off U), hence s-finite. By Tonelli (Mathlib measurable_measure_prodMk_left, MeasureTheory/Measure/Prod.lean:97), a ↦ μ(Prod.mk a ⁻¹' E_t) = μ(B_t(a)) is measurable ℝ^N → [0,∞]. Consequently a ↦ densityRatio n μ a t = μ(B_t(a))·(ω_n·ofReal(t)^n)^{-1} is measurable (product with a constant).

Step 4 (Borel representative). Define Θ(a) := liminf_{k→∞} densityRatio n μ a (1/(k+1)) ∈ [0,∞] (liminf along atTop). By Step 3 each a ↦ densityRatio n μ a (1/(k+1)) is measurable, and [0,∞] is a conditionally complete linear order with second-countable order topology and Borel σ-algebra, so Θ is measurable (Mathlib Measurable.liminf, MeasureTheory/Constructions/BorelSpace/Order.lean:1058).

Step 5 (agreement a.e.). Let x be as in Step 2. Since 1/(k+1) → 0 (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat) and 1/(k+1) > 0 for every k, the sequence k ↦ 1/(k+1) tends to 0 within (0,∞), i.e. along 𝓝[>] 0. Composing with HasDensity n μ x θ_x gives densityRatio n μ x (1/(k+1)) → θ_x, so Θ(x) = θ_x (Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq). Therefore Θ(x) ≠ ∞ and HasDensity n μ x (Θ x). This holds for μ-a.e. x (Step 2), so Θ is a measurable function with ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Θ x ≠ ∞ ∧ HasDensity n μ x (Θ x). Since N, n, U, V (with locally bounded first variation) were arbitrary, DensityExistsAE holds.
